scope: Inhibin B sex comparisons in minipuberty and chronological ages 8–20 years. The new female puberty reference is restricted to that comparison; existing global profiles, laboratory norms, Tanner observations and patient history are unchanged.
sourceFilesPolicy: Full primary articles and the original female infant supplement were inspected. No complete PDFs, copyrighted figures, participant data or private local paths are redistributed.

sources.location: Figure 3, p 1565; Methods and hormone assays
sources.population: 119 healthy term singleton Caucasian boys followed postnatally in the COPENHAGEN Minipuberty Study, Denmark, 2016–2018; 338 postnatal serum samples. Total paper population 128 includes 9 cord-only boys.
sources.assay: Beckman Coulter Inhibin B Gen II ELISA, A81303, RRID AB_2827405
sources.statistic: Age-specific GAMLSS median, approximately reconstructed from the vector PDF; not the separately modelled normalized longitudinal mean trajectory.
sources.independentVerification: A separate extraction using the original black central path and axis endpoints differed from all 359 active integer-day source knots by at most 0.083 pg/mL; both are approximate readings of the same figure, not author numerical coefficients.
sources.caution: The paper's 119-day peak of the modelled longitudinal mean is a different statistic. Stored decimal precision exceeds the source figure resolution; graphical quality guards are not LOD, LOQ or normal limits.

sources.location: Figure 1 and original supplement Table C
sources.population: 98 healthy term singleton Caucasian girls in the COPENHAGEN Minipuberty Study; 266 serum samples, median 3 per girl (IQR 1–4), observed from 5 days to 14.2 months.
sources.assay: Beckman Coulter Inhibin B Gen II ELISA, RRID AB_2827405
sources.statistic: Age-specific GAMLSS median from the original numerical supplement, not the biphasic normalized longitudinal mean trajectory.

supplement.table: C; median column, selected ages 0.02–1 years
supplement.independentTranscription: All 99 current inhibin B median values exactly match Table C. The supplement has 121 rows, ages 0–1.2 years; this change does not enlarge the active subset.

sources.caution: The Table C median has one broad peak. Do not add two peaks from the separate mean-trajectory analysis or treat model medians as observations at every age.

sources.title: Serum Concentrations of Inhibin B in Healthy Females and Males Throughout Life
sources.publication: Journal of Clinical Endocrinology & Metabolism 110 (2025), 70–77; first published online 26 June 2024
sources.location: Figures 1–3, Methods, menstrual cycle and oral contraception results, assay supplement
sources.statistic: Approximate digitization of the central GAMLSS model curve, labelled median/0 SD. Original L/S coefficients are not recovered; no author SDS or centiles are calculated.

female.population: 889 participants and 1005 samples in the full model; the COPUS II cohort includes 648 girls aged 5.6–20.2 years. Other cohorts include 92 infants and 149 adults.
female.assay: Serum Beckman Coulter Inhibin B Gen II ELISA for all female samples
female.interpolation: PCHIP using all 24 existing source nodes; the source-node domain is not the patient qualification domain.
female.cycleLimit: The age model is not standardized by cycle phase. Oral contraception affects concentrations; contraceptive status was unknown in part of the control sample. This is not a phase-specific or untreated-only norm.

male.population: 1818 participants and 2007 samples in the full model, including cohorts spanning ages 6.1–15.6 and 6.1–20.2 years.
male.assays: Serum Oxford Bio-innovation (917 samples) and Gen II (1090 samples), pooled in the source model
male.assayLimit: The source did not factorize pooled results using the reported overall Oxford/Gen II ratio 1.28. This implementation also applies no such conversion.

sources.caution: Figure 3 supports a common concentration axis but does not harmonize assays. Digitization tolerances are not confidence intervals, assay precision or normal ranges. Chronological age cannot assign breast/genital Tanner stage; published stage medians remain separate observations.

presentation.meaning: Equal height means equal concentration. Limits are a display choice, not laboratory reference limits or detection thresholds. Both periods retain the same axis regardless of patient, selected sex, result or marker eligibility.

mini.pointPolicy: Use the existing own-sex infant qualification. A seven-day boy can have a point before the common curves start. Neither sex receives a comparison point at exactly one year; no Kelsey substitution and no change to the female profile elsewhere.
mini.termPolicy: Term birth must be established for these infant point profiles. Preterm or unknown status prevents the point, not the population curves; corrected age does not qualify a premature infant.

puberty.pointPolicy: Evaluate the patient's own sex through the existing reference engine with the isolated comparison reference data. Female point eligibility is newly enabled only in this view and age window; the other sex's assay must not block a compatible own-sex point.

presentation.offScale: Zero is a valid point on the linear baseline; above 400 pg/mL use an upward arrow with the real number, without rescaling. Negative/invalid or censored values do not create an exact dot. Numerical tolerance at an axis boundary is not a clinical threshold.
presentation.centralReference: Patient concentration and own-sex source median are evaluated independently. Do not force either onto another sex's line or an unrelated smoothed lifespan illustration.

controlValues.precision: Extra digits support reproducibility, not clinical measurement precision. Infant intermediate ages use the existing source interpolation.
syntheticContracts: Female puberty comparison ages 8 and 20 are eligible in a compatible context; below 8 or above 20 are not. Ordinary views do not gain this female profile.
An age interval crossing a comparison boundary is not reduced to its midpoint to create a point.
Empty, 0, 400, 1000 and cleared results preserve identical lines and scale; 0 and 400 are boundary points, 1000 is an upward arrow.
400 ng/L and 400 pg/mL are equivalent. No newly invented assay-conversion factor is used.
Unsupported own assay/material, known contraindications and censored results retain existing engine restrictions. Curves remain population context when a point is unavailable.

unchangedObservationalPanels.meaning: Separate medians and IQR at nominal day 7 and month 3, term/preterm and sex groups; not an arbitrary-age trajectory or a norm.
unchangedObservationalPanels.assayLimit: Serum Beckman Coulter ELISA, generation not specified; LOQ 5.2 pg/mL. Do not assume Gen II or splice these visits into the term-infant GAMLSS curves.

unchangedObservationalPanels.meaning: Separate male genital-stage medians, older plasma ELISA, including GH-treated short-stature participants. Neither an age assignment nor a replacement for Borelli age medians.
Existing older-age group means remain independent; not a source for the two comparison windows.

reproduction: Build readable data through build_runtime.py, retaining all original global source profiles and units.
Call VildaHormoneLifespanDisplay.buildInhibinComparison(data, referenceEngine, period) for mini/puberty; both models must use the same fixed linear scale and the documented source IDs.
Compare the scoped female profile's full 24-point array against inhb-digitized-median.json before PCHIP; only qualification is restricted to 8–20.

Evaluate each synthetic own-sex context through the real reference engine using the comparison model's referenceData, then enforce view/profile identity. Do not verify with a copied interpolation formula alone.
Check point/line invariance across empty, valid, off-scale and cleared results, own-sex assay independence, first birthday, 8/20-year boundaries and no female global-profile activation.
clinicalLimits: This is educational population context, not a diagnostic rule, normal range, personalized target or cross-assay calibration.
Source median, individual concentration, longitudinal mean trajectory, Tanner median, IQR and reference interval are different statistics.
The source checks and owner approval do not constitute clinical validation; implementation tests must exercise the actual production functions.
